args.rationale: Applying the firm's personal jurisdiction test to SCENARIO 2 (proposed Ohio suit against Brumfeld Freight Lines, a Georgia carrier), an Ohio court does not have personal jurisdiction. Brumfeld is not domiciled in Ohio (it is a Georgia citizen), so general jurisdiction fails. Specific jurisdiction also fails because the purposeful-contacts prong is unsatisfied: Brumfeld has no operations, customers, employees, or solicited business in Ohio, and its only connection is a single driver passing through Ohio in transit on an unrelated Pennsylvania-to-Kentucky route. Under the memo, such merely fortuitous transit presence does not count as a purposeful contact, and a defendant with no purposeful activity in the forum whose only connection is unrelated transit satisfies neither prong. The nexus prong also fails independently: the loading-dock injury to Ostrander's purchasing agent arose entirely at Brumfeld's Savannah, Georgia terminal during a site visit, entirely outside Ohio, and does not arise out of or relate to any Ohio contact. Because the defendant is not domiciled in Ohio and both the purposeful-contacts and nexus prongs fail, personal jurisdiction is lacking; the filing is rejected.
